messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: high rate of SRV lookup failures for service=backend.redwood.internal in us-east-1a. Symptoms: internal service calls to backend returning 502/504 and increased latencies for UI reads. Paging oncall-sre.

oncall-sre: acked. I'm on it — paging rajiv (network) and alex (platform). Can someone paste recent coredns logs?

alex: seeing a spike from CoreDNS in us-east-1a. Logs: 
```
2026-03-15T10:12:05Z plugin/errors: 2 errors: lookup _backend._tcp.redwood.internal on 10.0.0.10:53: i/o timeout
2026-03-15T10:12:06Z plugin/etcd: consul SRV get failed: context deadline exceeded
2026-03-15T10:12:07Z health check: 503 returning upstream errors
```

marta: quick runbook check — SRV lookup failure usually either coredns nodes overloaded, consul health issues, or cross-AZ routing flaps. Any recent autoscaler activity in that AZ?

rajiv: yep, autoscaler in us-east-1a had a burst of scale-downs ~10:08 which coincides. I'm seeing high packet drops on the overlay (eni) for the coredns nodes — probably flapping interfaces during scale events.

oncall-sre: can we mitigate quickly? Impact: some customer-facing reads and internal control-plane calls are degraded. Estimated customer impact: ~12% of requests to a subset of tenants see transient 5xxs, no major data loss.

alex: quick mitigations we can do now: 1) bump coredns replicas in us-east-1a, 2) evict and restart the two flapping coredns pods, 3) temporarily route cross-region service discovery to us-east-1b.

marta: ordering steps — do 1 and 3 in parallel. rajiv, can you scale the coredns daemonset?

rajiv: running: 
```
kubectl -n kube-system scale deploy/coredns --replicas=6 --context=us-east-1a
rcli network mark-az unhealthy --az us-east-1a --service-discovery
```

deploy-bot: Command accepted: scale deploy/coredns -> 6 replicas. Rolling update started.

leah: I'm patching the routing policy to prefer us-east-1b for backend SRV queries: 
```
routingctl set-priority --service backend --from us-east-1a --to us-east-1b --weight 0.8
```

oncall-sre: also clear coredns cache after pods come up: alex, can you hit the debug endpoint?

alex: hitting admin API after pod restarts: `curl -s http://10.0.1.23:8080/clearCache` -> 200 OK. Confirmed caches cleared. Also restarted consul agents on two border nodes to ensure fresh SRV registration.

marta: good. Observability: error rate dropped from peak 28% SRV failures to ~3% after reroute and scale. Latency back to normal for most tenants. Still seeing a small tail of failures for long-lived connections that cached bad responses.

oncall-sre: customer impact update: affected customers are predominantly those pinned to us-east-1a ingress. Outbound cross-AZ calls were getting 10-15% 502/504. No customer data loss.

rajiv: root cause preliminary: aggressive node autoscaler activity in us-east-1a caused transient network interface churn on nodes running critical control-plane sidecars (coredns/consul), resulting in DNS resolution timeouts and stale SRV lookups. Need follow-up: tune autoscaler cooldown and move critical infra to protected node groups.

marta: putting follow-ups in a ticket: (1) protected node group for coredns/consul, (2) autoscaler cooldown tweaks, (3) health check improvements to detect node NIC flap earlier, (4) postmortem within 48h.

oncall-sre: on-call handoff: I'm handing this to alex for carry-through. alex, you have it — please watch for any regression in the next 2 hours.

alex: taking it. I'll keep an eye, and start the postmortem doc. Notifying support to follow up with affected customers.

oncall-sre: INCIDENT STATUS UPDATE: mitigated -> partial recovery. Routing fallback and coredns scale worked. Continued monitoring.

(15m later) alex: monitoring shows SRV failure rate at 0.8% and error budgets intact. Rolling back temporary routing weight to default in 30m if stable.

(30m later) oncall-sre: last check — system healthy, no active pages for 20m. I'm closing the incident channel. Follow-up actions logged in ticket INF-2026-042. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

marta: noted for postmortem. Assigning owners in the ticket: rajiv (network), alex (platform), leah (routing).

incident-bot: Incident closed by oncall-sre. Summary: SRV lookup failures in us-east-1a caused by node NIC flaps during autoscaling -> mitigated by scaling coredns, clearing cache, and temporary routing to us-east-1b. Follow-ups filed.
